Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

spend verb

money

also spend money, lay out, pay out

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.4.68: operam, cūram, pecūniam impendant in eās rēs (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 6.15.9: dē vestrō impendātis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 383

impendō, impendere, impendī, impēnsum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

spend, lay out (money, effort)

With in and the accusative of what the money goes on. The cost itself is impēnsa or sūmptus.

Other words

  • īnsūmō, īnsūmere, īnsūmpsī, īnsūmptum — spend (on something)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Gell. 2.24.11: sēstertiōs trīcēnōs in cēnam (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • sūmptum facere — spend money, go to expense

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 6.2.4: omnīnō nūllus in imperiō meō sūmptus factus est; Cic. Fam. 12.30.4: sūmptum in rem mīlitārem facere (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • illud, mī Tīrō, tē rogō, sūmptū nē parcās ūllā in rē, quod ad valētūdinem opus sit

    this I beg of you, my dear Tiro: don’t spare expense on anything your health needsCic. Fam. 16.4.2

  • praestābō sūmptum nusquam melius posse pōnī

    I promise you the money could not be better spent anywhereCic. Q. fr. 3.1.3

  • Quantum in calceōs impendistī?

    How much did you spend on the shoes?composed

  • tempus (operam, pecūniam) impendere in (+ acc.)

    to spend time (effort, money) onTraupman 383

See also money, buy, pay, cost a lot, spend.
